title: Standard Operating Procedure: Slicing an Apple into Sections and Slices

steps.purpose: Confirm the apple is fit for use and get set up for the first cut.

actions: Pick up the apple and examine it for bruises, blemishes, or other defects.
Confirm the apple is whole and suitable for cutting.

decision_points.condition: a bruised spot is found on the apple's skin
decision_points.response: plan to cut on the bruised side of the apple first

decision_points.condition: the apple is inspected and found whole with no concerning defects
decision_points.response: proceed to cut the apple without alteration

actions: Hold the apple upright on the board with one hand.
Bring the knife into position at the side of the apple with the other hand, ready to cut.

steps.step: Cut a section from the apple
steps.purpose: Separate a large section from the apple or core piece so it can be trimmed and sliced.
steps.repeats: Repeat for each section cut from the apple (typically twice per apple, working around the core piece).

tasks.task: Position the apple or core piece for cutting
actions: Hold the apple or core piece upright in one hand, presenting an uncut face toward the blade.
Adjust your grip so the stem is clear of the intended cut line.

decision_points.condition: the apple's stem sits in the path of a straight cut
decision_points.response: angle the cut beside the stem rather than straight through the top of the apple

actions: Press the knife blade into the top of the apple or core piece, beside the stem if needed.
Draw the blade straight down through the apple in one stroke, cutting a section free from the core piece.
Lift the section and core piece apart slightly to check the cut.

decision_points.condition: the cut is running close to the core
decision_points.response: keep the cut away from the core to avoid slicing into it

tasks.task: Inspect and set aside the core piece
actions: Turn the core piece to inspect its cut face for bruising.
Set the core piece aside on the board (e.g. top-left), skin side up, and keep it for cutting the next section.

decision_points.condition: the cut face shows minor bruising
decision_points.response: judge it acceptable and continue without further action

steps.purpose: Reduce each section into individual slices of consistent, usable size.
steps.repeats: Repeat for each section of the apple, and for each slice cut from that section.

actions: Hold the section upright in one hand, cut face oriented toward the blade.
Draw the blade down along the rounded or blemished edges of the section, cutting away thin scraps of skin.
Set trimmed scrap aside, separate from the slices.

decision_points.response: cut away the scrap of skin covering the bruise before slicing

decision_points.condition: a mark on the skin looks like frost rather than bruising
bruising on the cut face turns out less severe than expected
decision_points.response: continue cutting the section as normal

actions: Start cutting from the bigger end of the section; avoid starting from the smaller end, as this makes it harder to judge the size of each cut and to see it clearly while cutting.
Cradle the section in one hand, presenting a fresh face to the blade.
Press the knife down through the section in a single stroke, cutting a slice free.
Guide or let the slice fall onto the board, joining the fan of slices.
Rotate the section slightly in hand after each cut to present a new face, and repeat until the section is reduced to a small remnant.

decision_points.condition: a slice starts coming out bigger than the others but is still within tolerance
decision_points.response: judge it acceptable and continue cutting the same way

decision_points.condition: a cut slice is judged too thin to count as usable product
decision_points.response: set it aside as scrap instead of keeping it with the slices

decision_points.condition: the remaining piece of the section becomes too small to cut further
decision_points.response: set it aside as scrap rather than continuing to cut it

decision_points.condition: the remaining piece looks small but is judged still large enough
decision_points.response: cut one more slice from it rather than discarding it

actions: Periodically check both sides of the blade to confirm each slice is a consistent, correct size before making the next cut.
Use the flat of the knife blade, or the fingers, to nudge the fanned slices into a tidy row on the board as they accumulate.

decision_points.condition: the cut slices are spreading unevenly across the board
decision_points.response: nudge them into a tighter, aligned row using the flat of the blade or fingers

steps.purpose: Finish work on the apple by clearing scrap, core piece, and slices from the board.

actions: Place the final slice into the fan of slices.
Withdraw both hands from the board, leaving the finished pieces in place.

tasks.task: Remove scrap and pieces from the board
actions: Lift the scrap from the corner of the board and carry it off the working area.
Lay the knife down flat near the edge of the board.
Gather the fanned slices and carry them off the board.
Lift the remaining scrap pieces and the core piece off the board in turn.
Sweep any remaining slice off the board, leaving only the knife.

synthesis_notes: Merged run1's 'Prepare the apple' step and run3's 'Preparation' step into one 'Prepare the apple' step; run2 did not show an inspection phase, so this step is recorded as observed in 2 of 3 runs.

Collapsed the alternating 'section then slice' phases that occurred twice per apple in each run (once per section) into two looping steps, 'Cut a section from the apple' and 'Cut slices from the section', each carrying a repeats field, rather than listing each pass as a separate step.

Collapsed the long sequences of individually numbered slice cuts (up to twelve per section in run2) into a single looping action within the 'Cut slices from the section' task, since each cut followed the same pattern.

Demoted run1's 'Establish cutting technique' task (a single narrated aside about starting from the bigger end of the section) into an action within the 'Cut slices from the section' task, since it is a technique note rather than a distinct unit of work.

Demoted run2's 'Maintaining knife and checking technique' step (scraping the blade against the slices as a self-check) into the 'Check and tidy the slices' task, merging it with the tidying decision point since it is the same physical action performed for a dual purpose.

Folded run1's 'Check cut sizes while cutting' task and run2/run3's standalone inspection asides ('Further inspection and slice judgment', 'Handling bruised piece') into decision points and actions within 'Cut slices from the section', since each was a single in-line judgment call rather than a separate phase of work.

Standardized differing step and task names across runs (e.g. 'Section the apple', 'Cut a section from the apple', 'Divide the section into smaller pieces') into the canonical steps 'Cut a section from the apple' and 'Cut slices from the section', and applied canonical nouns (section, core piece, slice, scrap) throughout.

Merged run1's 'Trim scrap from the remaining piece' and 'Conclude the slicing' tasks with run3's trimming actions under 'Divide the section into smaller pieces' into a single 'Trim scrap from the section' task, since all describe removing scrap material from a section before or during slicing.

Retained 'Clear the board' as the standard closing step even though it was only fully demonstrated in run3; run1 left finished pieces on the board and run2 explicitly paused 'intending to do another run', so this step's observed_in_runs reflects a single full demonstration while still representing the logical end of the procedure.
